thread_messages:
luis (Sales): Quick async check — Pulsewell dedicated pilot: customer asked for HSM-backed key management + VPC peering checklist. PO pending but they want trial start next Wed. Need security/eng ETA on onboarding and any PRs we should fast-track.

emma (Sales): Pipeline update: legal + procurement looped. They want a sample network diagram and expected time to full lock-in. Billing lead asked about SLA for Dedicated.

kevin (Solutions): Quick Q — do they require customer-managed HSM (on-prem) or cloud KMS with HSM-backed keys? They mentioned FIPS 140-2 and attestation.

anna (Security): If it's customer-managed HSM we need HSM vendor + certs, and a comms plan for key escrow (if any). For cloud KMS, confirm region and KMS provider (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault). Also need an MFA/SSO narrative for their security reviewers.

devon (Eng oncall): We can support both options, but timelines differ. Rough estimates: cloud KMS integration + VPC peering: ~3 business days after we get KMS account ARN, contact IPs, and required ports. Customer-managed HSM (on-prem) with private link + cert exchange: ~7-10 business days (depends on vendor support). Also need target qps and model footprints to size Dedicated pool.

matt (Eng Infra): Heads up — PR #4512 (vpc/peering: allowlist + routing policy) is in review; unblocked if we get quick approvals. Pinging @jenna to triage the CR. deploy-bot: New PR assigned — #4512 (vpc-peer-routing)

jenna (Eng): on it, will jump on the review today and flag any infra work. If we approve, we can merge and stage the peering changes in the staging account.

luis (Sales): Thanks — can someone drop a minimal ACL + port list I can send to Pulsewell's infra team? They want an exact snippet for their firewall team. Also need a phrasing for the security PO about HSM attestation.

devon (Eng oncall): Dropping a minimal example below — share as-is.

```
# Example allowed egress (customer -> redwood)
# Customer egress CIDR: 10.40.0.0/22 (example)
# Required ports:
# 443 TCP -> api.redwood-inference.prod (TLS)
# 7150 TCP -> kv-cache.redwood-inference.prod (gRPC)
# 9000 TCP -> metrics/health (internal)

ALLOW from 10.40.0.0/22 to api.redwood-inference.prod:443 TCP
ALLOW from 10.40.0.0/22 to kv-cache.redwood-inference.prod:7150 TCP
ALLOW from 10.40.0.0/22 to metrics.redwood-inference.prod:9000 TCP
```

devon (Eng oncall): For the HSM attestation wording: "Redwood supports HSM-backed key wrapping via [vendor]. We require exchange of vendor attestation documents and customer-provided public key material. Redwood's control plane will not retain unencrypted key material. Detailed integration steps provided upon intake."

anna (Security): Good start. Add: "Customer must provide FIPS 140-2 level and vendor attestation; Redwood will perform periodic access audits and provide logs upon request."

luis (Sales): Perfect — I'll send both to their security contact. PO update: procurement expects to route PO by EOD Friday if no extra contracts.

kevin (Solutions): Small ask — Pulsewell asked if we can reserve a 2xA100 equivalent for the pilot window. What's the capacity request to make that guarantee?

devon (Eng oncall): If they need 2xA100 steady, we can reserve on Dedicated as a burst pool through the Dedicated booking flow. Need official request (start/end dates + expected concurrency). We'll validate model footprint.

luis (Sales): I'll collect dates and approximate concurrency. Thanks all — pinging back once customer confirms. :thumbsup:

matt (Eng Infra): FYI I left a couple of inline comments on #4512 about route priority — should be quick.

jenna (Eng): reviewing now, intend to approve after small tweak.

luis (Sales): One last thing — is there any known latency impact for KV cache traffic over VPC peering? Customer asked.

devon (Eng oncall): Minimal — peering adds ~1–3ms typical; we do local routing + keepalive. We'll provide a small perf note in the intake packet.

luis (Sales): Awesome, that's everything for this check-in. I'll update the thread when PO arrives.
